subject: spring-boot
summary: Spring Data JPAのリポジトリパターン、@Transactionalの動作と伝搬規則、N+1問題の原因と対策、遅延/即時ロードの注意点を解説する。
key_points: @Transactionalは成功時に自動コミットし、RuntimeExceptionでロールバックする（検査例外はデフォルトでロールバック対象外）。
N+1問題は遅延ロードされたコレクションをループ内でアクセスすると発生し、Fetch Joinまたは@EntityGraphで解決する。
JPAのダーティチェッキングにより、トランザクションコミット時にエンティティのフィールド変更が明示的なsave()なしで永続化される。
misconceptions: @Transactional rolls back on all exceptions including checked exceptions by default.
@Transactional works on private methods the same as public methods.
You must always call save() to persist changes to a managed entity within a transaction.
check_questions: What is the N+1 problem and how can it be prevented?
When does @Transactional trigger a rollback by default?
What is JPA dirty checking and why does it allow updates without calling save()?

fact_candidates: Default rollback behavior of @Transactional (RuntimeException only, not checked exceptions)
FetchType.LAZY loads related entities only when accessed, not at query time
practical_judgment_candidates: Identifying N+1 queries in code that loops over entities with lazy collections
Choosing between Fetch Join and @EntityGraph for solving N+1
error_interpretation_candidates: LazyInitializationException when accessing lazy collection outside transaction
Silent data loss when @Transactional on private method is ignored by Spring proxy
scenario_candidates: Code review: loop accessing lazy collection — count total SQL queries issued
Entity field modified without save() — explain why the change persists
common_wrong_answer_patterns: Believing checked exceptions cause automatic rollback with @Transactional
Thinking @Transactional on private methods works via Spring AOP proxy
